De la boulangerie de Vairao à l'architec: From the bakery in Vairao to international digital architecture
My first job wasn't code. It was running an artisan bakery in Vairao, where I learned what no school can teach: keeping a business standing, day after day, with real customers and constant pressure.
Puis la vie a changé de direction sans m: Then life changed direction without asking me. An unplanned change brought me to France for several years. Rather than endure this interlude, I chose to fill it: a degree in psychology, two years of medicine, and a return to my first love, web development, which I was already doing at fifteen. This time, I came back to it with a fine understanding of how people work, at the dawn of a new era: the age of AI.
C'est en fondant Natural Beauty Vahine,: It was while founding Natural Beauty Vahine, designed to give Polynesian artisans an e-commerce showcase, that I identified the real problem: tools designed for mainland France simply didn't work in French Polynesia. That friction point has been my mission for three years: building solutions accessible to the people of the Fenua, without complexity or prohibitive costs.
Cette mission m'a menée à fonder Hinova: This mission led me to found Hinova Digital, then to co-found the Rū-fau-tumu Academy, to pass on to others what I learned by building everything on my own, from the Fenua.
Aujourd'hui, ce site n'est pas un simple: Today, this website is not just a portfolio. It is proof that rebuilding, when taken seriously, becomes an architecture.
